clue.text: Follow old times first make some soup

indicators.note: first says the old-and-times letters come before the following word

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: tradition first, then get the soup going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts O (old) and X (times) ahead of TAIL (follow).
explanation.definitionFit: Oxtail is a thick brown British soup made from beef tail.

clue.text: This dish crops up in some letters from readers

indicators.note: crops up means appears, so the dish's letters appear inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: A dish keeps being mentioned in the letters page of a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crops up in' points to the run inside 'some letters'; 'from readers' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a dish of beaten eggs cooked flat in a pan.

clue.text: Arouse bird, not well after having had food

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
ill means not well
ate means had food

explanation.surface: Someone excited by a bird after recovering from illness and a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' here belongs to the surface: the pieces simply run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or stimulate, especially pleasurably.

clue.text: Covered with cake decoration and chilled

definitions.meaning: a cake with a sugar topping has been given that treatment
made cold, as with a drink over cubes of frozen water

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a cake topped with sugar coating, and a drink made cold.

clue.text: Masses of frozen stuff with lettuces

definitions.meaning: floating mountains of frozen water at sea
the crisp round lettuce variety sharing the name of those floating masses

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: huge floating blocks at sea, and the crisp salad variety.

clue.text: Munching cook hasn't finished part of bird

indicators.note: the cook word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a chef is a cook
a wing is part of a bird

explanation.surface: A cook eating while still preparing a piece of chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' drops the last letter of CHEF to give CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing is grinding food with the teeth, as in munching.

clue.text: Advocate smoked ham with game

parts.note: to back a cause is to advocate it
gammon is cured or smoked ham

explanation.surface: Someone recommending smoked ham served with venison or pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like meat, beside ham; it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game of dice and counters for two players.

clue.text: Cooking stove's operating limits

definitions.meaning: a large kitchen cooker with several hobs and ovens
the span within which something works, such as a weapon's reach

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a large kitchen stove, and the extent within which something works.

clue.text: Cutlery used for courses at Gleneagles

definitions.meaning: eating utensils with bowls on handles
Gleneagles is a Scottish golf resort; the spoon was an old wooden golf club

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: table utensils, and old-fashioned lofted golf clubs used on links courses.

clue.text: Ale and wine put before the Queen

indicators.note: put before places the wine ahead of the royal letters

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Drinks being served to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark brown beer, a kind of ale.

clue.text: Terence to arrange for steak

indicators.note: arrange tells us to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking a man named Terence to organise the steak dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link: TERENCE TO is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecote is a boneless cut of beef from between the ribs.

clue.text: Preserve tips of dried onions? I'll see to it

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins

indicators.note: tips are the leading letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A cook offers to pickle the dried onions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips of' takes the first letters of 'dried' and 'onions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Can do is an informal promise that a task will be handled.

clue.text: Fish taken from lobster creels at night

indicators.note: taken from signals letters lifted out of the run of these words

explanation.surface: A night fisherman finds something else in the lobster pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' points inside 'lobster creels'; 'at night' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Horsey group have been reported supplying leguminous plant

parts.note: a string is a group of racehorses kept by one stable

indicators.note: reported means the next word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the word been, said aloud

explanation.surface: Racehorse owners say they have been providing animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner or French vegetable with long edible pods is a legume.

clue.text: Hunt for a drink (but change the order) before setting off

definitions.text: Hunt for a drink (but change the order) before setting off

parts.words: Hunt for a drink (but change the order) before setting off
parts.note: reorder the opening to read a drink for a hunt, taken before riders set off, traditionally while mounted

explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a drink given to riders on horseback before a hunt sets off.

clue.text: It makes bread brown, so treat differently

indicators.note: differently says these letters are rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A suggestion to handle a treat in a new way.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance that browns slices of bread with heat.

clue.text: Spring lamb go wild

indicators.note: wild says these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A springtime lamb running wild in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to leap or frisk about playfully, as to spring.

clue.text: Brown egg supplier in SE London

definitions.meaning: a breed of chicken that lays brown eggs
a suburb in the south-east of Greater London

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a chicken breed named after the place, and the suburb in Kent's corner of Greater London.

clue.text: Keep jam in a special area

definitions.meaning: to keep is to maintain or save
fruit boiled with sugar and kept in jars
a restricted area kept for one group, as a game reserve

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: maintain, a fruit conserve, and a protected territory.

clue.text: Drink up, swallowing recipe, which is shred to pieces

parts.note: tea is a drink
R is short for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finishing a cup while eating, then shredding the recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear something up is to rip it into small pieces.

clue.text: He preserves food using a mess recipe

parts.note: a pickle is a mess, a predicament
R is short for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook making food last by following a messy recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who preserves vegetables in vinegar or brine.

clue.text: Butcher's cleaver found in aircraft

definitions.meaning: a heavy blade for cutting meat
slang for a helicopter

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a chopping blade, and informal slang for a helicopter.

clue.text: Open when crystallised, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: candied fruit is crystallised in sugar

explanation.surface: Something opened once it has been sugared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' gives the sound of CANDIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and honest, as in open.

clue.text: Expert on spasmodic reaction derived from vinegar

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A specialist on twitches and what causes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the sour component of vinegar.

clue.text: Coffee is better before cup is overturned by Nico, drunk

indicators.note: before puts the outdo word ahead of the rest

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: overturned means the word cup is turned upside down, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: drunk shows the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunken man named Nico knocks over a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is overturned' gives PUC; 'drunk' gives CINO from NICO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an espresso topped with frothy milk.

clue.text: Amount of milk informally put up at a pinch

indicators.note: put up in a down light means the run is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a nip is a pinch

explanation.surface: Milk served sparingly, only in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ATNIP into PINTA. A pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, from milk adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a pint of milk, from a famous British advertising slogan.

clue.text: They feed travellers in both halves of the country

parts.note: taken as written
N and S, north and south, the two halves of a country

explanation.surface: Food for travellers found everywhere in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves are the north and south, abbreviated as N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelries offering travellers food and lodging.

clue.text: University chaps change their order for list of courses

indicators.note: the clue gives university then chaps; their order is swapped

parts.note: men are chaps

explanation.surface: Students swapping their selection of courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change their order' puts MEN before U.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes, or courses, of a meal.

clue.text: Mixer providing a boost of the first degree

definitions.meaning: a drink added to spirits, as with gin
something that invigorates
in music, relating to the first note of a scale

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: quinine water for gin, a pick-me-up, and the keynote in music.

clue.text: Aristocratic title of Elizabeth's th's favourite cheese?

definitions.text: Aristocratic title of Elizabeth's th's favourite
definitions.meaning: Robert Dudley, Earl under that title, was Elizabeth I's favourite
a red English hard cheese named after a Midlands county

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'th's' looks like a stray repetition; the clue reads Elizabeth's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the earldom of Elizabeth I's favourite Robert Dudley, and the red English cheese.

clue.text: Baskets of food follow cold drink

indicators.note: follow puts the baskets after the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
hampers are baskets of food

explanation.surface: Picnic baskets come after a cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAMPERS is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for champagne, the sparkling wine.

clue.text: Fruit — one of five delivered in a group to church

parts.words: one of five delivered in a group
parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A quintuplet delivers fruit to church.
explanation.definitionFit: A quince is a hard yellow pear-shaped fruit.
